blocks.text: Lipids are a class of organic compounds in animals and plants that includes fats and oils, phospholipids (as in cell membranes), steroids and terpenes (essential oils). Unlike polysaccharides and proteins, lipids are not polymers: they have no repeating monomer unit. They are hydrophobic but soluble in organic solvents. Lipids act as fuel molecules, signal molecules, membrane components, hormones and messengers inside cells. They are classified as simple, compound and derived lipids.

blocks.prompt: Why are lipids not called polymers?
blocks.explanation: They are not built from a repeating monomer unit.

items: Lipids: fats, oils, phospholipids, steroids, terpenes; hydrophobic; not polymers.
